claims.statement: The EUDR requires due-diligence information including the country of production and geolocation of all relevant production plots.
A plot associated with deforestation or forest degradation can disqualify relevant products from being placed on the market or exported.

contrary_evidence: The Regulation establishes operator responsibility; buying an evidence pack does not transfer that duty or prove negligible risk.

economics.acquisition_route: Unvalidated: one producing-region cooperative at a time, distributed to Polish and EU importers through customs brokers and specialist traders.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario, not a forecast: validate 5,000 plots in year 2, reach 5 million PLN ARR by year 5, build 4 million PLN founder equity and cash by year 7, and 5 million PLN founder net worth in years 8-10.
economics.founder_time: Unvalidated operating estimate: 2-4 hours per day after regional data collection is handled by contracted local operators.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated: 55%-80% gross margin after cooperative payments, satellite checks, translation and exception handling.
economics.payback: Unvalidated: 15-30 months because upstream onboarding precedes importer volume.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated commercial figures, including capital_required_pln: 150-600 PLN per lot plus 20,000-80,000 PLN annual importer access.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Unvalidated: repeat follows every shipment and production season; importer and cooperative retention are unknown.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Recurring plot histories, corrections and shipment outcomes reduce exception cost and raise switching costs
fingerprint.customer: EU importers and traders of in-scope commodities lacking durable upstream plot evidence
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Upstream cooperative agreements on supply; customs brokers and commodity traders on demand
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Contractually sourced, versioned lot-to-plot evidence with geospatial exception handling
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: An importer pays when a shipment evidence pack is delivered and for ongoing network access
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A shipment must be tied to production plots before being placed on or exported from the EU market

founder_fit: Uses geospatial data and anomaly detection.
Can focus on systems while local collection is contracted.
B2B broker distribution avoids public-facing marketing.
risks: False plot or chain-of-custody data creates serious customer exposure.
Scope or timing changes can delay demand.
Cross-border data collection may require more social and field operations than founder fit allows.

structure.control_point: Multi-season data-rights agreements with producer cooperatives and a lot-to-plot evidence lineage
structure.critical_dependency: Reliable upstream identity and chain-of-custody data, lawful contracts, current EUDR scope and credible geospatial validation

thesis: Secure recurring, consented access to plot geometries and production records through producer cooperatives, then provide lot-bound provenance evidence to EU importers via customs brokers and commodity traders. The moat is lawful upstream data access and correction history, not a surface-level due-diligence dashboard.
title: EUDR Upstream Plot-Evidence Cooperative
uncertainties: Importer willingness to trust a new evidence provider
